# Raw bidi control characters in tracked files (app#501, Trojan Source).
#
# internal/sourcehygiene/bidi_test.go fails when a tracked text file holds a RAW
# (encoded) U+202A-U+202E or U+2066-U+2069. Write the character as an escape
# instead: "\u202e" in Go, \u202E in YAML/JSON, {U+202E} in a case table, or
# U+202E in prose. An escape is ASCII and is never flagged. Attack data does not
# need a raw character: the repo's fixtures and test expectations all use escapes.
#
# This list is the exception, and it is a CLOSED SET:
#   - one entry per line: <path><TAB><reason>. The path is exact (no glob, no
#     directory, slash-separated, relative to the repo root). The reason is
#     required: what the raw character is for, and why an escape cannot do it.
#   - an entry whose file holds no raw bidi character is a FAILURE (a dead entry
#     would hide the next one), as is an entry for a file that is absent, binary
#     (a file with a NUL byte is not scanned) or listed twice.
#   - adding a line needs review (security-engineer, review-5x R1). Do not add a
#     line to make a red test green: change the file to use an escape.
#
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. There is no entry today.
